title: Loganin promotes diabetic wound healing and inhibits NLRP3 inflammasomes in diabetic mice via IL17/NF-kappaB signaling.
authors: Zhou, Jian; Ma, Zhouji; Ding, Youjun; Yan, Xin; Tan, Qian
one_liner_zh: 该文研究马钱苷通过IL17/NF-kappaB信号通路促进糖尿病伤口愈合，虽含分子对接但核心是炎症机制与湿实验，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic wounds are a common complication and a debilitating condition of diabetes mellitus, which are characterized by chronic inflammation, persistence, and aggravation. Evidence suggests the beneficial influence of Loganin on diabetic complications and inflammation. However, the effectiveness of Loganin on diabetic wounds remains uninvestigated. METHODS: Network pharmacology was applied to identify the potential targets of Loganin in diabetic wound healing. Employing a streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic mouse model, we conducted evaluations pertaining to the effects of Loganin on wound healing and assessment of macrophage-related phenotypes via ELISA, immunohistochemistry, Western blot and qPCR. In vitro, we used J774A.1 mouse macrophage cell line and induced differentiated Th17 cells for experiments. Molecular docking, biotin-labeled pull-down assays and cellular thermal shift assays were applied to investigate direct mechanisms. RESULTS: Loganin topical application accelerated wound healing in diabetic mice, reduced local inflammation, and inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation. The IL-17/NF-kappaB signaling pathway was suppressed by Loganin, thus inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome. In particular, Loganin inhibited IL-17 A/F production in Th17 cells and targeted the NF-kappaB p50 subunit in macrophages, thus blocking its nuclear translocation and pro-inflammatory activation. CONCLUSION: Loganin may be considered as an adjuvant or a new therapeutic agent in the management of chronic non-healing diabetic wounds.
abstract_zh: 背景：糖尿病创面是糖尿病常见的并发症，也是一种使人衰弱的疾病状态，其特征为慢性炎症、持续存在及加重。证据表明，马钱苷（Loganin）对糖尿病并发症和炎症具有有益影响。然而，马钱苷对糖尿病创面的有效性尚未被研究。方法：应用网络药理学（network pharmacology）识别马钱苷在糖尿病创面愈合中的潜在靶点。采用链脲佐菌素（streptozocin, STZ）诱导的糖尿病小鼠模型，我们通过ELISA、免疫组织化学、Western blot和qPCR评估了马钱苷对创面愈合的影响及巨噬细胞相关表型。体外实验中，我们使用J774A.1小鼠巨噬细胞系和诱导分化的Th17细胞进行实验。应用分子对接（molecular docking）、生物素标记的pull-down实验和细胞热位移实验（cellular thermal shift assay）来研究直接机制。结果：马钱苷局部应用加速了糖尿病小鼠的创面愈合，减少了局部炎症，并抑制了NLRP3炎症小体激活。马钱苷抑制了IL-17/NF-kappaB信号通路，从而抑制NLRP3炎症小体。特别地，马钱苷抑制了Th17细胞中IL-17 A/F的产生，并靶向巨噬细胞中的NF-kappaB p50亚基，从而阻断其核转位和促炎激活。结论：马钱苷可被视为管理慢性不愈合糖尿病创面的辅助或新型治疗药物。
